draft.title: Words for talking about texts
card: Metalanguage is the set of terms we use to talk about texts. Using exact terms makes a response clear and precise.
the voice that tells the story. A narrator can be a character or an outside voice.
the time and place where the story happens, such as a city street in winter.
a big idea the text explores, such as courage or belonging. It is not the plot, which is what happens.
draft.remember: Metalanguage gives you exact terms, so your response says clearly what you mean.

a.q: Which term names the time and place where a story happens?
a.why: Setting is the time and place of the story. Theme is a big idea, so it is not about where or when. The narrator is the voice telling the story.

b.q: Leila says her story has a boy who loses his dog, and that its theme is loyalty. What does she mean by theme?
opts: The big idea the story explores
The events that happen in order
The voice that tells the story
The place where the story happens
b.why: Theme is a big idea, here loyalty. The boy losing his dog is the plot, which is what happens, and that is the tempting wrong option. Narrator and setting are different terms.
b.clue: Leila names an idea, not an event.

b.best: The big idea the story explores
